Connect Home Assistant once, then choose the features you need.
Pair your Echo in Android’s Bluetooth settings and enable media audio. Test music playback on the tablet first.
Keep this device and Home Assistant on the same local network. Select a discovered address or enter your own.
Use the base address only, without /lovelace, /dashboard or other paths.

In Home Assistant: Profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token. Name it TAFA Device Bridge, then select Generate QR code in the creation dialog.
The token and its QR code are shown only when you create it. Scan before closing the dialog. If it is already closed, create a new token.

Check the saved address, token and HTTP permission, then start the player again.
Plays a silent local loop while the player runs. It may reduce Echo’s “Playing from…” prompts after idle. Results depend on the Echo; this can affect Alexa music and battery use.
Use either this keepalive or the HA dashboard keepalive. Turn it off if normal Alexa playback is affected.
Keepalive paused · restart the player to retry

1. Open Connect, select Home Assistant and scan the one-time token QR code from your HA profile.

2. Pair your Bluetooth speaker and test media playback in Android.

3. Start the player for audio output, or open Wakeword for optional local microphone recognition. Camera settings are available from Status.

4. Return to your compatible TAFA dashboard for voice requests. Keep the relevant Android service notification active.

TAFA Device Bridge uses the existing Echo Relay audio integration. The matching HA backend and dashboard must be installed separately. Each tablet keeps its own device ID for multiroom wakeword settings.

The prompt is generated by the Echo itself. Keepalive can reduce idle gaps but cannot guarantee that Echo announcements are suppressed. Stopping the player also stops its keepalive. Nothing starts automatically after a reboot.
If Android stops the player while idle, check this app’s battery settings and allow background activity if needed. Keep the tablet powered for continuous operation.
This stops the player and removes the saved server address, HTTP permission and encrypted token. To revoke the token itself, delete it in your HA profile.
Scan or enter a token before starting.

Share the front or rear camera with HA, optionally report image movement, or run a local camera test.
Choose a camera, then tap Start. Access is requested only then. Preview and test images stay on this screen; leaving it switches the camera off and clears the image.
No test image. Images are kept only in memory.
Test image from %1$s · %2$d × %3$d · on this device only

In HA, use camera.echo_relay_tablet for images and Jarvis Tablet Audio: Describe camera for the local vision model. Select your outdoor/door camera in the integration options. Image movement is a simple pixel comparison and can react to lighting; it does not recognize people or objects. Continuous capture needs power and may need Android battery settings adjusted. Nothing starts automatically after a reboot.
No camera is available on this device.
Camera could not be used. Another app may be using it, or this device may not support the preview. Stop other camera apps and try again.
Camera access was not granted. You can allow it in Android app settings and tap Start again. Audio works without camera access.
Scan cancelled. Your existing token was not changed.
Token scanned. Start the player to save it encrypted.
Bluetooth audio bridge · tap to open

Send the selected camera to HA at the selected refresh interval using your saved HA login. This continues when you return to the dashboard or switch the screen off. Start explicitly and stop here or from the separate camera notification. Images are not recorded. Install the matching Jarvis Tablet Audio camera receiver in HA first.
HA camera active · images are arriving
Save your HA address and token in audio setup first. Camera access does not require a running audio player.
Image delivery interrupted · retrying. Check Wi-Fi and HA. Old images expire in HA after 15 seconds.
HA camera access denied. Use a valid administrator token belonging to the paired HA user.
Install/update the Jarvis Tablet Audio camera receiver in HA, then reload that integration.
Another tablet is paired. Stop it and use the HA action Jarvis Tablet Audio: Unpair camera before pairing this device.
Camera image could not be prepared. Stop and restart the HA camera.
Camera active · sending images to Home Assistant
Requires a dedicated Home Assistant user for this room. Enable only after provisioning the room in Home Assistant. Restart the player to apply.
Stored on this tablet. Changes apply during the next capture cycle. Actual delivery may be slower depending on capture, upload and server load.
Recognizes Alexa, Jarvis or Hey Jarvis locally. Home Assistant receives a wakeword event and the dashboard handles the question. The configured handoff pause releases the microphone for Whisper.

Optional German model (~45 MB). Download it once on this device. Recognition audio stays local. Turn off the dashboard’s own wakeword detector before using native recognition; Alexa may also trigger an Echo.
Allow microphone access to test wakeword recognition.
This is a hypothesis-confirmation count, NOT an audio volume or decibel threshold. 1 = more sensitive, 3 = fewer false activations but possible missed calls.
Settings are synchronized per device with Home Assistant. Muting releases the Android microphone while the service stays running. Changes take effect after the next sync.
Could not save wakeword settings to Home Assistant: %1$s
Unlimited tablets: each installation gets a unique random ID. Enter a room name, start native recognition and select/pair the tablet in TAFA under Voice & Audio. No numbered slot restrictions.
Audio playback, native microphone and camera in one place.
Home Assistant, access token and Bluetooth. Set up once on this device.

Only using wakeword recognition? Switch to Wakeword and start it there; the same connection is saved.
